awarenessScore.ruleDescription: Awareness score = (number of knowledge questions answered at the defined awareness level ÷ 5) × 100. Items: Q3 familiarity ≥ moderately; Q4 able to identify at least some items; Q5 at least partially aware of impacts; Q9 has used an authorized facility; Q11 aware of a campus collection facility. This is an ad-hoc composite for descriptive comparison only — it is NOT a validated psychometric scale, and each item is weighted equally regardless of difficulty.

findings.title: Familiarity with the term e-waste is not universal
findings.body: 8.3% of respondents reported being "not at all familiar" with the term e-waste (10 of 120).

findings.title: Environmental and health impact awareness
findings.body: 64.2% reported at least partial awareness of the environmental and health impacts of improper e-waste disposal.

findings.title: Most common disposal route
findings.body: The most frequently reported disposal method is "Store at home (unused)" at 30% (36 of 120).

findings.title: Share using responsible channels
findings.body: 15.8% reported giving unused or damaged electronics to an authorized recycler or a campus collection point.

findings.title: Campus collection facility awareness gap
findings.body: 45.8% were not aware of any e-waste collection facility on campus, and a further 28.3% had heard of one but did not know where it is.

findings.title: Leading barriers to responsible disposal
findings.body: Top reported barriers: No convenient collection point (32.5%); Lack of awareness (30%); Facility too far / hard to reach (26.7%).
findings.basis: Q13 (multiple selection; percentages of 120 respondents who answered this item)

findings.title: Willingness to use a campus facility
findings.body: 78.3% said they would definitely or probably use a designated campus e-waste collection facility (94 of 120).

findings.title: Support for awareness campaigns
findings.body: 75% found campus awareness campaigns very or somewhat useful.

findings.title: Knowledge of uncontrolled incineration risks
findings.body: 63.3% correctly identified that burning or incinerating e-waste under uncontrolled conditions releases toxic fumes and pollutants (76 of 120).

findings.title: Knowledge of landfill contamination
findings.body: 70.8% correctly identified that landfill disposal may contaminate soil and groundwater (85 of 120).

findings.title: Reported knowledge of health effects
findings.body: The most frequently recognised health effect of hazardous e-waste exposure is "Skin irritation" (38.3% of 120 respondents answering this item; multiple selections allowed).
findings.basis: Q18 (multiple selection; percentages over 120 respondents who answered this item)

findings.title: Awareness of hazardous pollutants
findings.body: Most-recognised pollutants released during improper handling: Lead (47.5%); Mercury (37.5%); Dioxins and furans from certain uncontrolled burning processes (27.5%).
findings.basis: Q19 (multiple selection; percentages over 120 respondents who answered this item)

findings.title: Environmental components recognised as affected
findings.body: Components most often selected as affected by improper disposal: Soil (36.7%); Air (35%); Plants and wildlife (35%).
findings.basis: Q20 (multiple selection; percentages over 120 respondents who answered this item)

findings.title: Composite awareness score (descriptive)
findings.body: Mean awareness score across the five knowledge items was 52.7/100 over 120 respondents. This composite is descriptive only and is not a validated scale.
findings.basis: Pre-defined rule applied to Q3, Q4, Q5, Q9, Q11

findings.title: Departmental coverage
findings.body: Responses span 9 departments/schools; the largest share is Civil Engineering (15%).

findings.title: Proposed: structured awareness programme
findings.body: If awareness gaps persist in the measured data, a short orientation module on identifying e-waste and data-safe decommissioning can be added to induction weeks. (Proposed intervention — not a measured result.)

findings.title: Proposed: visible campus collection points
findings.body: Clearly signed collection bins in hostels, departments, and the library, emptied on a published schedule by an authorized recycler. (Proposed intervention — not a measured result.)

findings.title: Proposed: authorized recycler partnership
findings.body: A memorandum with a CPCB-authorized recycler for periodic campus drives and take-back of damaged devices. (Proposed intervention — not a measured result.)

findings.title: Proposed: working-device donation channel
findings.body: A "rehome, don't discard" channel for functional old devices to juniors, labs, or community schools. (Proposed intervention — not a measured result.)
